sections.title: Understanding Level 2 Caselets
sections.content: In Level 2, the data is hidden within a paragraph and some values are not directly given. You usually solve it in 3–4 steps: (1) Extract – identify the given data, (2) Deduce – find the missing values, (3) Organize – create a table or Venn diagram, (4) Calculate – perform the final calculation. Questions often combine 3-set Venn diagrams, missing values from averages, and topics like Profit/Loss or Interest.

sections.title: 3-Set Venn Diagram (Only, Exactly, None)
sections.content:
Suppose there are 200 people in total. 120 like Cricket, 100 like Football, and 80 like Hockey. 40 like Cricket and Football, 30 like Football and Hockey, 20 like Cricket and Hockey, and 10 like all three sports.

Step 1: First place the number who like all three (10) in the center.
Step 2: Exactly two = (Cricket & Football) − 10 = 30.
Step 3: Only Cricket = 120 − (30 + 10 + 10), calculated carefully.

Note: "A and B" may include people who like all three, but "Only A and B" excludes the third group.

sections.title: Missing Data via Average/Total
sections.content:
The average marks of 5 students are 60. Marks of 4 students are 50, 55, 65, and 70.

Step 1: Total marks = 60 × 5 = 300
Step 2: Sum of four students = 240
Step 3: Marks of the fifth student = 300 − 240 = 60

Find the missing value by calculating the total from the average.

sections.title: Double-Layered Matrix Concept
sections.content:
Four cities – Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai. The number of mobile phones sold and the price per phone are given for each city.

Total Sales = Quantity × Price

If 100 phones are sold in Delhi at ₹10,000 each, total sales = ₹10,00,000.

To find overall sales, calculate sales for each city separately and then add them.

sections.title: Profit & Loss Integration
sections.content:
A shopkeeper bought 200 bags at a cost of ₹500 per bag and sold them at a profit of 20%.

Step 1: Total cost = 200 × 500 = ₹1,00,000
Step 2: Profit = 20% of 1,00,000 = ₹20,000
Step 3: Total selling price = ₹1,20,000

In Caselets, this data may be combined with cities or departments.

sections.title: Simple/Compound Interest Integration
sections.content:
₹50,000 invested for 2 years at 10% per annum simple interest.

SI = (P × R × T)/100 = (50000 × 10 × 2)/100 = ₹10,000

If it is compound interest, the principal changes every year. In Caselets, this may be connected with total investment or profit.

sections.title: A and B vs Only A and B
sections.content:
"A and B" can include people who belong to A, B, and C together.
"Only A and B" excludes the third group.

Understanding this difference is very important in Level 2 questions.

sections.title: 3–4 Step Solution Framework
sections.content:
Step 1: Extract – write down all numbers separately.
Step 2: Deduce – find missing values using averages or totals.
Step 3: Organize – create a Venn diagram or matrix.
Step 4: Calculate – compute only what is asked.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1. Including all three groups while calculating exactly two.
2. Not calculating the total from the average.
3. Forgetting to multiply Quantity × Price.
4. Applying profit percentage on Selling Price instead of Cost Price.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 2 Caselets include 3-set Venn diagrams, missing values, matrix-based sales calculations, and topics like Profit or Interest. Careful reading and proper organization are the keys to solving them correctly.

tricks.title: Place the Common (All Three) First
tricks.explanation: In a 3-set Venn diagram, fill the center (all three groups) first.
tricks.example: If 10 like all three, write 10 in the center.

tricks.title: Exactly Two = Pair − Three
tricks.explanation: Subtract the number of all three from the pair intersection.

tricks.title: Missing Value from Average
tricks.explanation: Total = Average × Number, then subtract known values.

tricks.title: Solve Matrix Row-wise
tricks.explanation: Calculate totals for each city or department separately.

tricks.title: Profit is Usually on Cost Price
tricks.explanation: Profit percentage is applied on cost price unless stated otherwise.

tricks.title: Remember the SI Formula
tricks.explanation: Use P × R × T / 100 for quick calculation.

tricks.title: None = Total − All Regions
tricks.explanation: Add all Venn regions and subtract from the total.

tricks.title: Identify Keywords
tricks.explanation: Pay attention to words like "Only", "Exactly", and "At least".
tricks.example: "Only A" means other groups are excluded.

tricks.title: Interconnected Variables
tricks.explanation: If price changes, total sales also change. Identify the relationship.

tricks.title: Do Not Skip Steps
tricks.explanation: Do not calculate directly without extracting and organizing data first.
tricks.example: Create a table first, then solve.
